Ready for the maintainer to merge. Safety-tier review: no blocking findings.

I read the full diff and the current laws from `upstream/main:AGENTS.md`.
There is no earlier review to resolve.

The joint guard limits both the gap and the endpoint shift relative to each arc's chord.
The margin includes the joint shift. The kerf and cover laws check the recorded path before generation returns it.
The new posted-program test checks five consecutive arc blocks and rejects motion blocks with no XY motion.

### Local build and tests

All commands ran locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-3988`. No GitHub runner ran.
The trial merge is `12c42aed3d4cca021ddb3ee404d206d75fc5452c`, with main `f287a370c81b60d24cfaf026cfa04afeb7943bbd`.
Its first parent is the exact PR head named above. The merge was clean.

### Extra suites run

I also ran these motion tests separately with `--exact`:

- `wire_edm::arc_tests::the_laws_catch_a_mutated_arc_path`: 1 passed.
- `wire_edm::arc_tests::tangent_arcs_join_arc_to_arc_with_no_connector_move`: 1 passed.

Mutation results:

- Circle arcs moved 2 um into the product: the kerf law refused the path. The test passed.
- Circle arcs replaced by straight chords: the cover law refused the path. The test passed.
- One oval arc moved 2 um into the product: the kerf law refused the path. The test passed.
- The unmodified circle and oval paths passed their safety checks.

No fixture directory or importer changed. The extra fixture and kernel STEP rules do not apply.
No UI code changed, so screenshots are not required.

### Goldens moved

None. I checked the changed-file list against the body.
The CL and wire-post golden tests passed without regeneration, including the ISO, Sodick, and G-EDM DXF arc goldens.

### Requested before merge

None. All tests run on this head passed. Full heavy lanes did not run, as the current review law requires.
The worktree and branch remain in place to retain the build cache.
The PR author is qsmits, so I leave the author's ready state unchanged.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
